person.name: Deepankar Jaisia
person.headline: Full-stack product engineer
person.summary: Full-stack product engineer with an AI/ML edge — an engineer who ships AI-integrated products at scale. 7 years of experience, currently at People Inc., with solo ownership across major platform initiatives: auth, comments and analytics.

orgs.name: People Inc.
orgs.subtitle: Formerly Dotdash Meredith
orgs.summary: Platform and product engineering across 45+ brand sites, including People.com at 20M+ DAU — auth, membership, migrations, analytics and growth.

projects.title: Auth Platform Rebuild
projects.summary: Rebuilt the login/auth platform's frontend so every brand site tracks the current core platform instead of lagging behind on stale published packages.
highlights: Moved the platform from an npm-dependency model to a git-dependency model — sites pull directly against current source, and the separate publish and hosting step is gone.
Each site's build package went from ~100 files (the whole project) to the ~15 config/SCSS files it actually needs.
Onboarded 5 sites — including Investopedia and the People app — ahead of a hard quarterly deadline, without waiting on a cross-team CI/CD change.
Wrote an onboarding skill and AGENTS.md documentation, plus a shared Slack channel; onboarding became mostly self-serve for other engineers.

projects.title: People.com Auth Launch — Incident Response
projects.summary: During the auth platform's first launch on People.com, account routes still resolved to the old, dead app. Diagnosed the layer at fault in a ~50-person war room.
highlights: Recognised the symptom from a near-identical incident months earlier, then confirmed from the served HTML that the new app wasn't being hit at all.
Narrowed it to CDN/edge routing (Fastly redirect rules) rather than application code — and pulled in Infra, who hadn't been on the release.
Fixed live with no rollback, so the new comments feature stayed up.

projects.title: Comments on People.com
projects.summary: Account templates and service integration for Viafoura comments on People.com.
highlights: Built the account templates that gather user info and connected the Viafoura comments service.
Flagged that protected-endpoint auth was happening client-side and pushed for the redirect-to-login logic to move server-side.

projects.title: Migration Squad
projects.summary: After the company merger, moved the last 10 brand sites onto the new internal platform on a 3-month deadline.
highlights: Executed the migrations while closing gaps in the existing playbook as real issues came up.
Re-sequenced a site whose team was near its own launch window instead of forcing the deadline, and documented that exception path.

projects.title: Membership Paywall Sprint
projects.summary: Brought in to build the navigation for a paywalled membership feature; took ownership of the cross-team branch merge and a caching bug nobody had root-caused.
highlights: Reconciled ~300 commits across two teams' branches, working directly with 6–7 engineers and using Claude to categorise commits by area.
Traced stale logged-in state through edge, browser cache headers and Redis down to the browser disk cache.
Removed caching for logged-in users and fixed the related bfcache issue — correct paywall state with no regression for anonymous users.
Shipped before the hard quarterly deadline.

projects.title: Southern Living Insiders
projects.summary: Owned the nav and footer for a new premium membership tier — shared sitewide components already juggling 15–20 combined states.
highlights: Added a new membership state without breaking existing combinations (newsletters, subscriptions, logged-in/out, saved recipes, scroll states).
Decided what logic belonged in the shared core codebase versus the brand's own code.
Consolidated variants into a single reusable component and worked with design to keep patterns maintainable.

projects.title: MyRecipes App Launch
projects.summary: App-download marketing pages for the MyRecipes app launch, with install tracking across our pages and a partner's.
highlights: Refactored copy-pasted page templates into a config-driven system — a new page is a JSON file.
Integrated AppsFlyer OneLink and QR codes so installs are tracked.
Technical point of contact for a third-party company building their own landing pages with the same tracking.

projects.title: Recipe Ticker
projects.summary: A continuously updating recipe ticker for MyRecipes.com, built while learning Vue.js on a hard deadline.
highlights: Infinite-feeling scroll with two 25-item lists: fill the off-screen list while the other is in view, then snap seamlessly.
Only 50 items in memory at any time, however long someone scrolls.

projects.title: GTM Tracking Standardization
projects.summary: Refactored how Google Tag Manager tracking is added to web components and introduced a sitewide tagging convention.
highlights: Wrote the documentation followed for migrating events across all sites.

projects.title: Resy × Amex Booking Widget
projects.summary: Picked up a partner-facing booking widget mid-flight while its engineer was on leave.
highlights: Finished the remaining functionality, including capping reservations shown with a “see more” pattern.
Got up to speed on the availability endpoint — our proxy in front of Resy's API.
Represented the team as the only engineer on the final call with Resy and Amex, and raised rate limiting on the backend's behalf.
Kicked off QA to keep the launch on track.

orgs.name: Hackathons
orgs.summary: Fast builds — work hackathons and NYC Vision Hack v2.

projects.title: RAG Support Agent
projects.summary: A retrieval-augmented pipeline that helps an internal support agent answer basic user questions. Started as a work hackathon project.
highlights: Tied for first place at the hackathon; now in daily use.
Tracked usage and cost per request (chunks retrieved, context size); a proper quality evaluation — golden set, retrieval precision, groundedness — is the next step.

projects.title: Axon
projects.summary: A real-time, multi-client notes app in the style of Obsidian/Notion, built in about 10 hours at a work hackathon.
highlights: Write-then-broadcast: writes POST to SQLite (source of truth), then the server pushes updates to every client over SSE.
Chose SSE over WebSockets — the write path and broadcast path were already separate.
Optimistic locking with version checks; the conflict policy depends on the caller (UI prompts the user, MCP retries once).
MCP server for AI agents to CRUD notes, revision history, a backlink graph view; one codebase for web and Electron.

projects.title: vibecheck.nyc
projects.role: Owned the entire client and data-serving layer
projects.summary: A live crowd-density platform for NYC that fuses permitted-events data with public DOT traffic cameras — a Gemini chat agent plus a real-time heatmap dashboard. NYC Vision Hack v2 (Google Cloud × Roboflow × Veris).
highlights: When Google deprecated HeatmapLayer mid-build, wrote a replacement from scratch: a canvas OverlayView with Gaussian-blob accumulation and a 256-entry colour lookup table, with zero added dependencies.
Real-time geospatial aggregation: each camera assigned to the nearest of 16 neighbourhood zones, with “× usual” density ratios against multi-day baselines.
Auth bridge to an IAM-gated Cloud Run service using GCP metadata-server identity tokens, proxying SSE agent responses and camera frames — shipped as one Docker deploy.

projects.title: SSO for a Regulated Client
projects.summary: Built a single sign-on integration using SAML/ADFS that met the client's compliance and security requirements.
highlights: Chose a full SAML/ADFS integration over a simpler auth flow because the client's compliance bar was non-negotiable.
